title: A power series ring over a characteristic-zero field or a Cohen ring is formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology
statement: Let $n\ge0$. (1) Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, $C=K[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], regarded as a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $\mathbf Q\subseteq K\subseteq C$, and $\mathfrak m_C=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. (2) Let $p$ be a prime, $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], $C=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ and $\mathfrak m_C=(p,x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Z$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9704), parts (1) and (3); part (2) (F_p -> L[[x]]) is not stated here. Its proof reduces by the universal property of power series rings to Q -> K formally smooth (Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322, proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions) and Z -> Lambda formally smooth for the m_Lambda-adic topology (Algebra, Lemma Tag 0329, lemma-cohen-ring-formally-smooth).

proof.text: Fix a test datum from [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]: a commutative R-algebra D, J with J^2=0, and g from the power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] to D/J killing the k-th power of the specified ideal, with k >= 1. The quotient q is the map of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Each variable belongs to the specified ideal, so g(X_i)^k=0. Choose d_i in D with q(d_i)=g(X_i). Then d_i^k belongs to J, hence d_i^(2k)=0. Put a=(d_i) in D and b=(g(X_i)) in D/J; unlike the original plan, a need not include p in the Cohen case. Each ideal is finitely generated and contained in the nilradical, hence nilpotent by Mathlib Ideal.FG.isNilpotent_iff_le_nilradical. A nilpotent ideal c with c^N=0 gives completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] directly: Hausdorffness follows at exponent N; for a compatible sequence f, use f(N) as its limit, compatibility for m<=N and equality f(N)=f(m) modulo c^N=0 for N<=m. The private helper complete_of_nilpotent proves this for any module M over the coefficient ring: c^N times the top submodule is zero, so the same stabilization argument applies. The private helper nilpotent_span proves nilpotence for a family indexed by any finite type, using finiteness of its range and Ideal.FG.isNilpotent_iff_le_nilradical. Their applications here specialize to the ring as a module over itself and the finite type Fin n, including n=0 and subsingleton target rings. These genuine generalizations avoid restating the private ring/Fin n helpers of the downstream PowerSeriesFieldCohenFsAdic module, which cannot be imported without a cycle.

proof.text: In the characteristic-zero field case restrict g to gK:K -> D/J along the constant-series map C. It is a Q-algebra map since ring maps preserve rational scalars. Use the Mathlib realization of [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-formally-smooth]: choose a transcendence basis s of K/Q by exists_isTranscendenceBasis; hs.isAlgebraic_field gives algebraicity over IntermediateField.adjoin Q (range s); characteristic zero implies separability over this intermediate field. Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_algebraicIndependent_of_isSeparable hs.1 gives formal smoothness of K/Q. Apply Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_lift J with nilpotence witness (2,hJ) to obtain a Q-algebra map h:K -> D whose quotient is gK.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9704), proof (line 9718): reduction (1) '$\mathbf Q\to K$ is formally smooth', by Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions, algebra.tex line 44475)

proof.text: In the Cohen-ring case [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], the constant series C(p) belongs to the specified ideal. Since g kills its k-th power, p^k=0 in D/J, so p^k belongs to J in D and p^(2k)=0 in D. Put I=span{p^(2k)} in Lambda. The restriction g.comp C kills I, by the quotient equality and multiplicativity, and therefore descends to gLambda:Lambda/I -> D/J by Ideal.Quotient.lift. Apply the explicit ring-homomorphism clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth] at exponent 2k (positive because k>=1), target D, and ideal J. It yields hbar:Lambda/I -> D lifting gLambda. Compose with Lambda -> Lambda/I to obtain h:Lambda -> D; Ideal.Quotient.lift_comp_mk verifies q.comp h = g.comp C.

proof.text: Given the coefficient lift h from either of the previous steps, the private helper lift_powerSeries performs the construction of Step 1 and applies [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to (D,a), coefficients h, and variables d_i. It obtains f from the power series ring to D, agreeing with h on constants and taking X_i to d_i. Apply the uniqueness clause of the same node in (D/J,b), with coefficients g.comp C and variables g(X_i). Both q.comp f and g agree with these coefficients and variables, so they are equal. Package f as an R-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]: for Q use RingHom.map_rat_algebraMap, and for Z use preservation of integer casts. The equalities of ring maps imply equality of algebra maps by extensionality.
